data.name: Yashoda
data.long_meaning: Yashoda is a Sanskrit name derived from the word 'yash', meaning wealth or prosperity. In Hindu mythology, Yashoda is the name of a devout woman who is the foster mother of Lord Krishna. The name symbolizes abundance, wealth, and prosperity. It is believed that a child named Yashoda will bring prosperity to her family.

in_sanskrit.name: यशोदा
in_sanskrit.long_meaning: यश् (yash) means prosperity, wealth, abundance, richness. दा (da) means giver or bestower. यशोदा (Yashoda) is the one who bestows prosperity.

in_hindi.name: यशोदा
in_hindi.long_meaning: वर्धना (vardhana) means one who nourishes, sustains. यश (yash) means prosperity, wealth, abundance, richness. दा (da) means giver or bestower. यशोदा (Yashoda) is the one who nourishes and bestows prosperity.

in_tamil.name: யாஷோடா
in_tamil.long_meaning: உழவர் (uzhavar) means lord, master, owner. யாஷ் (yash) means prosperity, wealth, abundance, richness. ஓடா (oda) means giver or bestower. யாஷோடா (Yashoda) is the one who gives prosperity.

data.cultural_impact: Yashoda is a revered name in Hindu culture, best known as the foster mother of Lord Krishna. She is an embodiment of pure love, devotion, and maternal affection. In Hindu literature, Yashoda is depicted as a beautiful, devoted, and righteous woman who is deeply devoted to her foster child, Lord Krishna. Her name is synonymous with selflessness, sacrifice, and unwavering devotion.
data.spiritual_significance: In Hindu spirituality, Yashoda represents the ultimate expression of selfless love and care. She is the epitome of a caring and nurturing mother, who is always willing to go the extra mile to protect and provide for her child. Yashoda is a source of inspiration for women, who are often tasked with the role of nurturing and caring for their families. Her story teaches us the importance of selflessness, devotion, and unconditional love in our lives. It serves as a reminder that by nurturing and caring for others, we can bring about wealth, prosperity, and happiness not only for ourselves but for those around us.

historical_references.reference: Yashoda is mentioned in the Hindu epic Mahabharata, as the wife of Lord Krishna and the foster mother of his son, the great hero Balarama.
historical_references.context: Mahabharata is an ancient Indian epic that forms a major part of Hindu mythology and Indian literature. It is a vast and complex work consisting of 18 books, and is believed to have been composed between the 4th and 2nd centuries BCE.

historical_references.reference: Another reference to Yashoda can be found in the Puranas, where she is described as the mother of Lord Krishna. According to this account, Yashoda was a cowherdess of Vrindavan, who was deeply devoted to Lord Krishna. When Krishna was a baby, she was given the responsibility of taking care of him, and she loved him deeply. One day, Krishna playfully lifted the Govardhana Hill as a prank, and Yashoda was very worried about him and reprimanded him.
historical_references.context: The Puranas are a set of ancient Indian texts that deal with various aspects of Hinduism, including mythology, history, philosophy, and ethics. They are believed to have been composed between the 4th century BCE and the 8th century CE.
